title: DNA Methylation Signatures Predict HIV Prognosis and Mortality
author: Xinyu Zhang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.smdec26

steps.title: Run EWAS meta‑analysis
steps.instruction: Combine discovery and replication EWAS summary statistics using METAL (version 2010‑02‑08) to perform a fixed‑effects, inverse‑variance meta‑analysis with sample size and standard error weighting; obtain effect sizes and p‑values for each probe from cohort 1 and cohort 2; assess heterogeneity between the two sample sets with the I² statistic.

steps.title: Remove batch effects
steps.instruction: Apply the removeBatchEffect function from the R limma package (version 3.32.10) to the methylation data to correct for batch effects arising from different processing times and platforms before any machine‑learning prediction.

steps.title: Select informative CpG probes
steps.instruction: Use the SmartFeatureSelection R package (https://bitbucket.org/starrcofly/smartfeatureselection.git) to filter irrelevant probes, rank probes by relative attribution, and reduce redundant signals by keeping CpG sites with false‑discovery‑rate (FDR) ≤ 0.05 or associated with good prognosis (VACS index ≤ 50).

substeps.instruction: Filter probes based on methylation‑association analysis results.
Rank probes according to their contribution to outcome prediction.
Retain only CpG sites meeting FDR ≤ 0.05 or VACS ≤ 50 criteria.

steps.title: Build greedy ensemble model
steps.instruction: Apply four distinct machine‑learning algorithms to the filtered CpG set, then combine their predictions using a weighted average (greedy ensemble) to create a single predictive model.

substeps.instruction: Train each of the four machine‑learning models on the training data.
Determine optimal weights for each model based on performance.
Compute the weighted average of the four model outputs to obtain the ensemble prediction.

steps.title: Validate predictive model
steps.instruction: Perform 10‑fold cross‑validation on the testing set to identify the best‑performing ensemble model, then evaluate that model on an independent replication cohort.

substeps.instruction: Split the testing set into ten folds and iteratively train/validate.
Select the model with the highest cross‑validation performance.
Apply the selected model to the replication sample for external validation.

steps.title: Construct methylation risk indices
steps.instruction: Create separate DNA‑methylation risk indices for hypomethylated and hypermethylated CpG sites using the published formula, then treat each index as either a categorical variable (highest quartile as reference) or a continuous variable (per‑standard‑deviation decrease).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the index for hypomethylated CpGs.
Calculate the index for hypermethylated CpGs.

steps.title: Test association with mortality
steps.instruction: Assess the relationship between each methylation index and all‑cause mortality using Kaplan–Meier survival curves with log‑rank tests, followed by Cox proportional‑hazards regression adjusting for age, antiretroviral therapy, HIV‑1 viral load, and CD4 count.

substeps.instruction: Generate Kaplan–Meier plots for each index and perform log‑rank tests.
Fit Cox models with the index as categorical (quartiles) and as continuous (per SD) predictors, adjusting for covariates.

steps.title: Perform pathway and network analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze genes nearest to the selected CpG sites with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA); for genes with multiple CpGs, use the lowest CpG p‑value to represent gene‑level significance; consider pathways significant if FDR < 0.05.
